analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1645-2464): scheduler configuration, prompt geometry, deadlines, MTP, sampling, reasoning parsing, and tool-call parsers. The PR's actual change is a documentation-only addition at head lines 3541-3575, a new section on cluster service listeners (ClusterService.listenerChange, ClusterSetupLinkExchange pairing identity, 5 s listenerCheckSeconds). That section is outside the supplied units, and its patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not verify it. The base text I examined contains no code or control changes. It touches trust-relevant areas only descriptively: MTP typical-acceptance output approximation, which is documented as non-distribution-exact and relevant to T-007 and T-056; prefix-cache identity not changing with the sampler, relevant to T-041; and the DARKBLOOM_CBV2_* override disqualification rule. None of this indicates a security regression. The documented cluster-listener behavior (pairing-keyed handshake rejection; the pairing identity comparison deliberately excludes the edge secret) is not in the supplied excerpt as source, so there is nothing to cite on the head side. A later pass should check whether the new cluster pairing and listener surface (a Mac-to-Mac setup exchange and control lease on the cable) is covered by a threat-model boundary. The canonical model has no cluster or distributed trust boundary among the indexed definitions, which may be a threat-model gap. The docs describe the refusal of mismatched pairings, but the authentication strength of the handshake and the edge-secret handling are unverified from this evidence.
